problem_text:
A logistics firm must dispatch a courier to collect sensitive documents from nine corporate offices.  
The offices are situated at the following map coordinates:  

Office Alpha: (38,5)  
Office Beta: (8,153)  
Office Gamma: (158,33)  
Office Delta: (161,82)  
Office Epsilon: (26,179)  
Office Zeta: (140,166)  
Office Eta: (88,49)  
Office Theta: (98,200)  
Office Iota: (198,199)  

Travel distances between offices, measured in kilometers, are predetermined:  

Alpha to Gamma: 123.2 km  
Alpha to Delta: 145.1 km  
Alpha to Epsilon: 174.4 km  
Alpha to Zeta: 190.6 km  
Alpha to Eta: 66.6 km  
Alpha to Theta: 204.0 km  
Alpha to Iota: 251.5 km  
Beta to Gamma: 192.1 km  
Beta to Delta: 168.7 km  
Beta to Epsilon: 31.6 km  
Beta to Zeta: 132.6 km  
Beta to Eta: 131.2 km  
Beta to Theta: 101.5 km  
Beta to Iota: 195.5 km  
Gamma to Delta: 49.1 km  
Gamma to Epsilon: 196.8 km  
Gamma to Zeta: 134.2 km  
Gamma to Eta: 71.8 km  
Gamma to Theta: 177.5 km  
Gamma to Iota: 170.8 km  
Delta to Epsilon: 166.2 km  
Delta to Zeta: 86.6 km  
Delta to Eta: 80.1 km  
Delta to Theta: 133.8 km  
Delta to Iota: 122.7 km  
Epsilon to Zeta: 114.7 km  
Epsilon to Eta: 144.0 km  
Epsilon to Theta: 75.0 km  
Epsilon to Iota: 173.2 km  
Zeta to Eta: 128.0 km  
Zeta to Theta: 54.0 km  
Zeta to Iota: 66.7 km  
Eta to Theta: 151.3 km  
Eta to Iota: 186.0 km  
Theta to Iota: 100.0 km  

Due to a security restriction, direct travel between Office Alpha and Office Beta is prohibited.  
Furthermore, owing to a contractual stipulation, the route must incorporate exactly one of two specified corridors: either the link between Office Beta and Office Gamma, or the link between Office Gamma and Office Delta.  

The objective is to determine the minimal total travel distance for a circuit that visits each office precisely once and returns to the origin.
